Performers
Beatrice Harrison (cello), Symphony Orchestra (orchestra, as on the labels), Edward Elgar (conductor) Documented

The archive quotes Moore on the ensemble’s New Symphony/Royal Albert Hall identity; the published credit follows the photographed labels rather than silently expanding their wording.

[1] [2] [3]
Work version
Four acoustic sides, one movement per side; the whole concerto is abridged. Documented

This is the abridged whole concerto, not the complete score or a sixteen-minute finale. The supplied stream already joins all four sides. Only a continuous early finale passage is aligned with the complete Skidmore finale; neither complete work durations nor omitted music are equated. The exact cuts and acoustic-session instrumental substitutions are not established, so no modern-score orchestra timeline is projected onto this recording.

[1] [4]
Recorded
22 December 1919; 16 November 1920 Documented

The later session applies to replacement side three, HO 4607-AF. The finale, HO 4198-AF, belongs to the December 1919 session; the listen ID names the two-session recording rather than dating every side to 1920.

[1]
Place
Hayes, Middlesex, England Documented

Source-reported session location, not inferred from the record manufacturer’s address.

[1]
Label
His Master’s Voice / The Gramophone Company Documented[2] [3]
Catalogue
D541; D545 Documented

The archive dates first issue to May 1921 for D541 and June 1921 for D545.

[1] [2] [3]
Matrix, take, sides
I: HO 4197-AF / 2-07853; II: HO 4194-AF / 2-07854; III: HO 4607-AF / 2-07855; IV: HO 4198-AF / 2-07856 Documented

The archive says take numbers are not indicated on the discs. It reports take 2 for side three and an additional take-2 attribution for side one from Moore; no take is assigned here to the finale.

[1] [2] [3]
Transfer
Unknown Unknown

No transfer engineer is identified; an uploader is not automatically the engineer.

Transfer date
Unknown Unknown

No transfer date is established; upload dates are not used as transfer dates.

Processing
Single supplied FLAC with MP3 derivative; archive reports a digital pitch adjustment to side three. Documented

The archive estimates A=435 Hz at 78 rpm for the earlier sides and A=430 Hz for side three before correction. This is not a verified original session tuning. No local concatenation or audio processing was performed.

[1]
Composition rights
Underlying Elgar composition is out of copyright under the ordinary life-plus-70 term. Inferred, not documented

The archive identifies Elgar’s dates as 1857–⁠1934. This term calculation does not clear a later edition.

[1]
Recording rights
United States public domain: recording first issued in 1921, before the 1926 cutoff. Documented

Programme rule 2. The item states May and June 1921 issues and cites contemporary reviews; its metadata and description contain no non-commercial licence. The eligibility is based on the issued sound recording, not the composition. No unrestricted modern restoration licence is invented.
